evals.prompt: Our backend has a 1,200-line server.py with models, authentication endpoints, and payment webhook logic all mixed together. Downstream unit tests import 'app' and several utility functions directly from server.py. Please audit the file and decompose it into clean modules without breaking existing imports.
evals.expected_output: The model detects Mode A (Single-File Fast-Track), audits server.py using code_health_audit.py, outlines cohesion clusters, implements the package facade pattern with __init__.py or server.py re-exporting public symbols, extracts routers and services into separate files under 300 lines each, preserves all docstrings/comments, and verifies with unit tests and code_health_audit.py.
expectations: Routes to Mode A (Single-File Fast-Track) without unnecessary multi-file project roadmap ceremony
Audits the target code using code_health_audit.py before and after changes
Maintains zero breaking imports by re-exporting moved symbols via facade or __init__.py
Keeps extracted files and classes within the quantitative modularity budget (<=350 lines, <=10-12 methods)
Preserves existing docstrings, rationale comments, and test compatibility

evals.prompt: We have a legacy web project with 8 huge files (database.py at 2,100 lines with 60 methods, app.py at 1,900 lines, worker.py at 950 lines, and several 1,000+ line JS/CSS files). I don't want to go file-by-file figuring out what to ask each time. Please refactor our project to follow a recommended modular structure and migrate it by parts.
evals.expected_output: The model runs code_health_audit.py, detects Mode B (PROJECT_CAMPAIGN), proposes a layered directory structure (Level 0 models/utils -> Level 1 repositories -> Level 2 services -> Level 3 routers/UI -> Level 4 facade entrypoints), creates a 4-phase dependency-ordered checklist in MIGRATION_LOG.md, updates AGENTS.md with a Monolith Freeze, and immediately executes Phase 1 Slice 1 with facade re-exports and test verification.
expectations: Runs code_health_audit.py and selects Mode B (PROJECT_CAMPAIGN) for multi-monolith repositories
Designs a layered target directory structure (models/utils, repositories, services, routers, frontend modules)
Persists a 4-phase dependency-ordered migration checklist in MIGRATION_LOG.md with [ ] checkboxes
Updates AGENTS.md with a Monolith Freeze and target directory ownership map
Executes or initiates Phase 1 Slice 1 using the 5-Step Zero-Regression Decomposition Workflow and checkpoints MIGRATION_LOG.md for automatic resume

evals.prompt: /refactor-monolith Continue migrating the next part of our project.
evals.expected_output: The model checks MIGRATION_LOG.md first (Mode B2 Auto-Resume), automatically identifies the next unchecked [ ] milestone without asking the user which file to pick, runs code_health_audit.py --show-methods on that target file, extracts the cohesive module with zero breaking imports, runs tests, and marks the item [x] in MIGRATION_LOG.md.
expectations: Reads MIGRATION_LOG.md first and automatically selects the next pending [ ] milestone without requiring the user to specify a filename
Runs code_health_audit.py --show-methods on the selected milestone file
Applies the 5-Step Zero-Regression Decomposition Protocol with facade re-exports
Verifies with unit tests and code_health_audit.py, then marks the milestone [x] in MIGRATION_LOG.md

evals.prompt: We have a 1,350-line frame_processor.py containing CLI parsing, config loaders, telemetry reporters, and a tight per-frame NumPy/OpenCV hot loop that shares pre-allocated buffers. We also hit circular import failures twice when a teammate tried splitting the hot loop earlier. Please use /plan (or our custom architectural planner) to plan the decomposition first, warn us if splitting any part would hurt performance, and define how to handle mid-refactoring failures or strategy changes without breaking anything.
evals.expected_output: The model honors the requested planning workflow (/plan or custom planner) before modifying production code, runs code_health_audit.py, warns that splitting the tight per-frame buffer hot loop across modules would degrade performance and memory locality, proposes a Hot/Cold split (keeping the hot kernel cohesive while extracting cold CLI, config, and telemetry helpers behind a backward-compatible facade), and defines the mid-execution anti-thrash stop-loss (halting on >=2 failures, advising safe revert of unstable edits, and escalating via /plan or /grill-me to pivot strategy).
expectations: Honors the user-specified planner (/plan or custom architectural planner) by presenting a structured pre-flight decomposition plan and waiting for approval before modifying production code
Explicitly warns about the performance and memory-locality degradation risk of splitting the tight per-frame hot loop across files, proposing a Hot/Cold split instead

Defines a mid-execution escalation and anti-thrash protocol that halts after repeated failures, advises reverting broken speculative edits, and pivots strategy or consults the user via /grill-me or /plan
Preserves 100% backward-compatible imports via a re-export facade while enforcing quantitative modularity budgets (<=350 lines, <=10-12 methods)
